title: Strip moved by a text: first and second differences of the forced key (12+10 and 11+9 letters) against 198,934 sculpture readings and as unknown English, on 666,993 dictionary tableaux
k4_result: 80,039,064 settings (666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort x 2 directions x 2-3 numberings from 0 or 1), each in three parts = 240,117,192 tests. Part A (known texts, exact): best placement 10 of 22 with the 42-letter gap (three settings tie), 0 of 22 with the gap free; 484 settings had three six-letter pieces somewhere in the texts and were placed exactly; 22 needed. Part C (second differences): best 10 of 20, 586 settings placed; 20 needed. Part B (unknown English): best fragment STOSESTKSISC|UNCHANTENV at -4.534 per quadgram (16 quadgrams), next NYEMADESESHA|KCANERDEST -4.726, SCMNATERNOCA|DEINECALSY -4.728; none of the best 15 reads as English.
controls: 5 shuffled K4s, all alphabets. Part A best: 9, 10, 12, 10, 11 of 22 (K4 10); settings placed 418, 487, 504, 494, 508 (K4 484); one shuffle reached 13 of 22 with the gap free. Part C best: 9, 10, 9, 9, 11 of 20 (K4 10); placed 590, 566, 584, 538, 626 (K4 586). Part B on 3 shuffled K4s: best -4.742, -4.461, -4.715 (K4 -4.534; one shuffle beats K4).
scope_limits: Tableau: A-Z, KRYPTOS, a dictionary keyword alphabet or one of its two transposition-mixed forms, in five layouts; hidden or non-dictionary alphabets are not covered. Moving text numbered on A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet, from 0 or 1, strip moved either way; no other numbering (no Caesar-shifted numbering, no reversed alphabet). Parts A and C are exact but only for the 198,934 readings of attack 58 (both panels, K1-K3 plaintext, Morse; rows, columns, diagonals, back-and-forth, reversed; every d-th letter, d up to 60; 9.86M letters), with block 2 exactly 42 letters after block 1 or anywhere in the same reading. The 'best of 22' figures are a gauge only: a setting is placed only when three six-letter pieces of its fragments occur in the texts, so partial matches without six letters in a row are not counted (a full match always is). Part B is weak: 16 quadgrams, and the noise top over 80M settings is -4.46 to -4.74, while the four planted English fragments scored -4.03 to -4.61; one planted answer won by 0.001. So an English moving text whose 22 letters score below about -4.5 would not stand out, and Part B rules out only clearly English fragments. Moving texts in German or another language, texts that skip spaces differently, a text that restarts or changes between the blocks, and third or higher differences are not tested. The clue positions are taken as exact.

negative.family: Sliding key moved by a text (running sum of a sentence or sculpture reading)
negative.hypothesis: K4's key is the running sum of a non-repeating text (each text letter says how far to move the strip), or the running sum of that running sum, on a dictionary keyword tableau.
negative.scope: 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort x both directions x text numbered on A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet from 0 or 1 = 80,039,064 settings. First differences (12+10 letters) and second differences (11+9) of the forced key placed exactly in 198,934 readings of the sculpture (panels, K1-K3 plaintext, Morse; rows, columns, diagonals, skips 1-60; 9.86M letters), blocks 42 apart or anywhere in one reading; first differences also scored as unknown English on the big model (16 quadgrams).
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: no known text fits (K4 best 10 of 22 and 10 of 20; 22 and 20 needed) and the best English-looking fragment is noise (-4.534, STOSESTKSISC|UNCHANTENV) (controls: 5 shuffled K4s best 9-12 of 22 and 9-11 of 20, 3 shuffled K4s best English -4.742, -4.461, -4.715; planted 6/6: K2 plaintext 22 of 22, panel column reading as second-order text 20 of 20, four unseen sentences ranked first of 80M settings at -4.03 to -4.61). The unknown-English part only excludes clearly English fragments (above about -4.4).

follow_ups: Make the unknown-English test of the moving text decisive by using more letters: for the top few thousand settings of Part B, extend the moving text outward from each block with a beam search on the big model (each added text letter gives one more key value and so one more plaintext letter next to EASTNORTHEAST or BERLINCLOCK) and score moving text AND plaintext together; a true setting grows two English strings at once, noise cannot. Planted: the four sentences of this run.

The same exact Part A test with German moving texts: the Weltzeituhr city ring and the Berlin texts of attack 80, numbered on A-Z/KRYPTOS/tableau alphabet; it needs only those texts added to kryptos.idea108_moving.text_streams.
